short: The day-to-day costs of running the business, below gross profit.
seoTitle: Operating Expense — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: The day-to-day costs of running the business, below gross profit. They are what gross profit has to cover. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Operating expenses are the day-to-day costs of running a business that are not part of the direct cost of sales — salaries, rent, marketing, utilities, repairs and administration. They are what gross profit has to cover.
bodyHtml:
Why Operating Expense matters

Operating expenses are where most cost control actually happens, because direct costs are largely set by suppliers and recipes. They also creep, since each addition looks small on its own.

Operating Expense formula

Operating profit = Gross profit − Operating expenses

Adding depreciation back gives an approximation of EBITDA.

How Operating Expense works in practice

Track them by category month on month rather than as one lump, so a rising line is visible early. Comparing each category as a percentage of sales makes growth-driven increases distinguishable from genuine drift.

faq.question: Is buying equipment an operating expense?
faq.answer: No. Equipment is capital expenditure, recovered through depreciation over its useful life.

faq.question: What is a healthy expense ratio?
faq.answer: It depends on the trade. Track your own ratio against last year rather than an external benchmark.
